signature_moves: Colonizes the MacBook notch dead-zone as the primary interactive surface — transplants the iPhone Dynamic Island / Control-Center Now-Playing schema onto macOS (Jakob's Law borrow); the top screen edge is an infinite-depth Fitts target
Album art is the only chroma in an otherwise monochrome true-black HUD; the lone red source badge is the 'which app is playing' signal (Von Restorff), and no user-accent is spent
Two independent floating-glass modules rather than one bar: an ambient-status notch panel and a separate navigation launcher pill, each its own Liquid-Glass surface
Concept-as-icon: the app icon renders the MacBook notch itself (black bezel + notch cutout wrapping a glowing blue concave interior) — the product thesis as one object
defects: Contrast Dilution (mild) — secondary label gray #717171 on true black ~4.2:1, just under 4.5:1 AA for the smallest metadata; canon secondary-on-dark is #FFFFFF@55% ~#8C8C8C
Truncation without ellipsis (low confidence) — queue titles clip hard at the panel's right content edge with no ellipsis or scroll-edge fade; could be marketing-crop framing

aesthetic.direction: Platform-native Liquid-Glass HUD in the Control-Center Now-Playing register — SF Pro monochrome on true black, album art as the only color, restrained committed-neutral palette; closest range-map family is neo-grotesque product (dark neutral + glass) but it is really Apple's own HUD grammar

psychology: Jakob's Law — deliberately mirrors the iPhone Dynamic Island / Now-Playing schema, so a Mac-first paradigm reads as pre-learned and requires no teaching
Fitts's Law — parks the HUD at the top screen edge (effectively infinite-depth acquisition target) and gives the launcher generous glass targets
Von Restorff effect — the single red source badge (and the album art) are the only saturated elements, so they carry the 'which app' signal pre-attentively
Aesthetic-Usability effect — polished Liquid Glass + full-bleed album art buy a strong ~50ms first impression
Hick's Law — the launcher reduces navigation to 3-4 clearly-iconed modules
notes: Only one image carried app UI (cover.png); no shot-*.* files were provided (meta.json gallery empty). The cover is a genuine over-the-desktop screenshot (app on the user's coastline wallpaper), NOT a device-frame composite, so it is real design evidence — but the capture scale is ambiguous (1816x568 crop, not a full logical screen), hence all geometry/type is estimated with wide ranges and only sampled hex is measured. icon.png was viewed for brand context (notch-as-object motif) but NOT digested under Workflow B per task scope. Lineage is 'native' at med confidence: no window chrome exists to confirm AppKit vs SwiftUI, but the SF Symbols set, Liquid-Glass launcher with container morphing, and true-black HUD material all read as a custom SwiftUI notch utility (NotchNook/Boring-Notch genre). Density and accent 'failures' in the native audit are HUD-appropriate conventions, not defects — flagged so a later synthesis pass does not treat this glanceable-large, monochrome register as general mac taste.
